chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Things happened to Boyd: the Washington players and Eddie Finckel
summary: Boyd never caused anything; the band turned jazz-oriented through the Washington players hired in its society days.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I am of the impression, having known Boyd, seeing the way he operated, that he never caused a damn thing to happen to himself, to his band. Things happened to him, and they happened by accident, they were caused by the men he would hire to work for him. If he hired a guy and the guy had any musical sense, the guy would recommend people who played in his idiom or his style, and the band would lean in
that direction. When he hired a few guys from Washington--this is after the society band--this is when the band changed from a society band to an impact band.
The Swope Brothers.
He got Earl and Ralph Rob Swope, Mert Oliver, Angelo Tompedis (phonetic spelling).
Angelo is going to be on the concert incidentally.
Right.
I told you.
Charlie Wolpe
Steven Jordan came on then too, I guess, at that time.
I can't think too much of Steve Jordan if he thought that Boyd was a good saxophone player.
He may have been terribly charitable to me too.
Could be.
He didn't know who he
was talking to.
Right; could be.

Things happened to Boyd. He didn't cause things to happen, they happened to him. He had the opportunity of rejecting them but he accepted everything that happened to him. When Washington dies, he changed his band into a jazz oriented band; he didn't stop it, he let it happen.
That was Eddie's doing, I guess. Eddie hired those people.
Fink.
Eddie's from Washington.
I didn't know that.
Maybe I shouldn't say that categorically. His sister lives there and he has ties there.
I know that they were close, Eddie with the Washington guys.
I think in fact he was born up in Rockville or something like that.
Anyway, he had ties in Washington, he had ties to all these people.

Right, but what I'm saying is that Boyd didn't go out hunting for Eddie, or hunting for the guys from Washington that played that way; they came to him and he accepted it, the same way the band changed when I started to write for him. It happened to him.
Were you instrumental on bringing the people on the band that were there?
Some of them. Most of them were there when I joined the band. Of course it changed as time went on. I wasn't that instrumental in bringing people into the band. I think I was responsible--
(Side B of Tape 3 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Tape 4.)
--I was responsible for what happened to the music.
The players themselves, I don't think I really brought any people in or insisted on him getting any. I stayed away from that. There may have been a few recommendations; I can't recall.
(Allen)
